author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 전국의 습지에서 흔히 겨울을 나는 겨울철새로, 하구와 호수, 하천에서 작은 무리를 짓는다. 잠수해 갑각류, 연체동물, 물고기, 수초 등을 먹는다. 번식기에는 호수나 습지 둘레의 숲에서 지내며 바위틈보다 숲속에서 번식하는 일이 잦고, 한배에 알 6~15개를 낳아 암컷이 27~32일 동안 품는다. 유라시아 대륙과 북미 대륙 북부에서 번식하고 유럽, 페르시아만, 캄차카에서 중국 동부, 한국, 일본, 알래스카에서 미국 중부에 걸쳐 월동한다.

art.subject: Common Goldeneye (Bucephala clangula), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean estuaries and lakes from November to March: large, peaked, triangular head glossy black with a green sheen; bright golden-yellow eye; a round white spot on the cheek between the eye and the bill base; neck, breast, flanks and belly white; back black; white scapulars with fine black stripes along the side of the back; tail blackish-grey. Short black bill; orange legs.
art.pose: swimming on open water in a small flock, about to dive
art.scene: Korean winter estuary with calm open water; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view swimming: peaked black-green head, yellow eye, round white cheek spot in front of and below the eye, white body, black back with black-striped white scapulars, black bill
adult female, side view swimming: dark chocolate-brown head, yellow eye, white collar, grey body, white belly, black bill with a yellow spot at the tip
adult male in flight, seen from above: black back, white inner wing (secondaries and coverts) contrasting with the black outer wing, dark head; head, body and tail held in one line
art.build: Stocky, compact diving duck, about 45cm, a little smaller than a Mallard, with a big head that rises to a peak on the crown and a short neck. Bill short, deep at the base and tapering, shorter than the head. Legs short, set far back, orange. Floats buoyantly and dives often. Flight fast with whistling wingbeats; the male shows a large white panel on the inner wing, the female a smaller white patch crossed by dark bars.
avoid: Do not paint a crescent-shaped cheek patch or a purple gloss with heavily black-marked scapulars; that is Barrow's Goldeneye (Bucephala islandica).
Do not give it a smooth round head; the crown rises to a distinct peak.
Do not paint a red or dark eye; both sexes have yellow eyes.
Do not place the white cheek spot behind the eye; it lies between the eye and the bill.
